description: Cross-binding conformance for the INDEXED LHS spelling of an ARRAY-shaped observed (esm-spec §6.3.1). §6.3.1 admits TWO LHS spellings for the equation that DEFINES an unknown — bare (`y ~ f(…)`) and indexed (`y[i] ~ f(…)`, which defines the whole array `y`) — and neither is restricted by rank: the defining form is read through the LHS's BASE NAME, so "an arrayed definition is observed exactly as its scalar counterpart is". Julia's tree-walk build classified equations by the SYNTACTIC `lhs isa VarExpr`, so an array-shaped observed written the indexed way matched no owner bucket and was refused outright with `E_TREEWALK_UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE` on a document Rust and Python both loaded (issue #232). Every array observed in this fixture uses the indexed spelling and is asserted DIRECTLY — that is what makes the category state the §6.3.1 contract rather than the intersection the bindings happen to agree on; the states they drive are asserted alongside, so answering the observeds while dropping them out of the dynamics (or the reverse) still fails. The observeds are a CONTROLLED PAIR: `wf` is STATE-FREE and `ws` is STATE-DEPENDENT, the two classes a binding routes differently, so fixing one path only does not pass. Both right-hand sides are exactly integrable — D(u) = wf = 2k is a per-cell constant giving u[k](t) = 2*k*t, and D(v) = ws = 3*u is then linear in t giving v[k](t) = 3*k*t^2 — so every solver family named below reproduces the goldens to machine precision and a divergence here is a semantics divergence, never an integrator one. PYTHON IS RED ON `main` AND GREEN ON PR #237 — the defect is fixed, the fix is not merged yet. It is kept in bindings_required rather than scope_excluded because it has a real runner: the category states the contract and lets the binding be red until the fix lands. Measured with #237's pkg/earthsci-ast-py/src on PYTHONPATH: main @ 71e25b380 scores 7/14, #237 @ 67504523 scores 7/14 (unchanged), and #237 @ 57b72acad scores 14/14. One root cause, three symptoms: `flatten._collect_model` read observed-ness from `classification.inlined_unknowns` — the strict `y ~ f(…)` set §6.3.1 sanctions for INLINING specifically — and used it as the classification, the same wrong substitution Julia's owner buckets made syntactically. The `red-on-main-until-pr-237` tag is documentation only: tags are free-form strings with no runner behind them, and the Python adapter deliberately carries no xfail (it would flip to an unexpected pass the moment #237 merges); drop the tag when that PR lands. See README.md and CONFORMANCE_SPEC §5.32.1 for the three symptoms and their reproducers. Julia is the reference binding: its `run_pde_tests` minted golden/observed_indexed_lhs.json.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator / inline PDE-test runner
